test_title: PYST 41: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 01 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Unemployment reflects the inability of the economy to provide jobs to those willing to work. Which organisation conducts the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**NSO (National Statistical Office)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** is conducted by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)** under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
 
• The **PLFS** was launched in **April 2017** to provide quarterly estimates of unemployment and labor force participation rates in urban areas and annual estimates for both urban and rural areas.
 
• The primary objective of the **PLFS** is to measure key indicators like the **Worker Population Ratio (WPR), Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), and Unemployment Rate (UR)**. Hence, the statement regarding PLFS being conducted by NSO is *correct.*
 
• The **NSO** collects data through household surveys, providing insights into **employment trends, sectoral distribution of workers, and gender-based workforce participation.**
 
• The survey is critical for formulating policies to address **unemployment** and improving **labor market conditions**. Hence, the statement regarding its economic significance is *correct.*
 
• The NSO relies on a scientifically designed sampling method, ensuring data accuracy and representation of diverse socio-economic groups across India.
 
• The **Ministry of Labour and Employment, RBI, and NITI Aayog** do not conduct the PLFS but may use its findings for policy-making or economic analysis. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is NSO (National Statistical Office).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Role of NSO:**

 
 
• **NSO** operates under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).** It is responsible for conducting large-scale surveys to collect official statistics on various socio-economic parameters.
 
• The **NSO** provides data on **employment, wages, household expenditure, health, education, and other vital indicators.**
 
 
 
• **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS):**
 
 
• The **PLFS** is the first of its kind survey launched in **India** to provide quarterly and annual estimates on labor force indicators.
 
• It focuses on understanding the **employment-unemployment scenario** and assists policymakers in designing strategies to address labor market challenges.
 
• **Example:** Data from the PLFS has been used to analyze the impact of events like the **COVID-19 pandemic** on employment in urban and rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Uses of PLFS Data:**
 
 
• The data helps in assessing the performance of various government schemes aimed at improving **employment levels**, such as **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA).**
 
• It also provides insights into sectoral trends, such as the **shift from agriculture to manufacturing and services** over the years.
 
• The data supports research and analysis for addressing issues like **gender disparities** in the workforce, informal sector employment, and regional variations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics of PLFS:**

 
 
• The **survey uses stratified sampling** to ensure representation from all sections of society, focusing on urban and rural areas equally.
 
• It provides estimates based on **age groups**, **gender**, educational qualifications, and other demographic factors.
 
 
 
• **Benefits for Policymaking:**
 
 
• The data from PLFS is critical for evaluating the success of initiatives like **Skill India** and addressing **regional unemployment variations.**
 
• It aids in tracking the impact of policies focused on **formalizing the informal sector** and improving job quality.
 
• Helps in designing targeted programs for **women empowerment** and increasing their participation in the workforce.
